newsitem.title: USA: Sparks chair sees 96/97 China corn exports 3.0 MMT. [CORRECTED 21:48 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Sparks chair sees 96/97 China corn exports 3.0 MMT. [CORRECTED 21:48 GMT]

text.p: Willard (corrects from William) Sparks, founder and chairman of agriculture consultant Sparks Companies Inc, Monday pegged China corn exports at 3.0 million tonnes in 1996/97 and said this could be a damper on U.S. corn exports.
Speaking to a food and agriculture policy conference sponsored by his company, Sparks predicted China corn exports "could easily be" 3.0 million tonnes in 1997/98 as well.

Turning to wheat, Sparks said he did not see an increase in U.S. wheat acreage in the future, noting U.S. wheat yields had been trending down and the research funds are "not there" for wheat, unlike for soybeans and corn.
"Overall, I don't see any big growth coming in wheat in this country," Sparks said.
He also said he did not see any big demand for U.S. wheat next year because of stiff competition from producers abroad.
"The U.S. is really going to be a residual supplier and we're not going to have much of an export demand," Sparks predicted.
